questions.question: A Prometheus server scrapes 400 targets, each exposing 1,500 post-relabel series. How many active series does the model budget?
questions.explanation: Active series equals targets multiplied by series per target: 400 x 1,500 = 600,000.

questions.question: Those 600,000 active series are scraped every 30 seconds. What is the modeled ingestion rate?
questions.explanation: Samples per second equals active series divided by scrape interval: 600,000 / 30 = 20,000.

questions.question: What does Prometheus's documented 1-2 bytes per sample estimate omit from a complete disk plan?
options: WAL, head, index and label shape, churn, compaction peaks, and operational headroom
questions.explanation: The formula estimates retained sample storage. Real capacity must include the mutable head, WAL, index shape, churn, compaction, and free-space policy.

questions.question: Which component evaluates an alert's PromQL expression?
questions.explanation: Prometheus evaluates alerting rules. Alertmanager receives alert state and applies grouping, routing, silencing, and inhibition.

questions.question: A remote-write endpoint is unavailable while the local TSDB is healthy. What should an operator expect first?
options: Remote-write queue backlog and retries while local ingestion can continue
questions.explanation: Remote write has a separate WAL-backed queue. An outage creates pending and retried sends and resource pressure before it necessarily affects local ingestion.

questions.question: Why does a classic histogram usually create more than one series for one label set?
options: It exposes cumulative bucket series plus count and sum series
It stores every request ID as a label
It evaluates one alert per bucket
It always duplicates data to remote storage
questions.explanation: A classic histogram exports a series for each configured bucket and also count and sum series, so bucket selection is part of the cardinality budget.
